question: What recall does hybrid (0.7 semantic + 0.3 BM25) retrieval achieve on CUAD?
lesson: Established the 61.4% recall@3 baseline with EmbeddingGemma (35.2% with NLEmbedding). Embedding quality matters: a 26-point gap between embedders. This is the number every retrieval idea is measured against.

question: Which embedding model is best for on-device CUAD retrieval, and does an absence instruction help doc QA?
lesson: EmbeddingGemma beat the alternatives tested. A plain 'if not in the sections, say so' instruction improved contract QA faithfulness. Prefer EmbeddingGemma unless a new idea beats it on a measured recall basis.

question: How many chunks (top-K) should be retrieved for Qwen doc QA?
lesson: K=3 chunks is optimal; more chunks added distractors and hurt answer quality. Ideas that increase retrieved context should justify why they beat K=3.

question: Can BM25-only match hybrid recall while removing the 600MB embedding model?
lesson: BM25-only recall was ~15 points below hybrid on CUAD; semantic embeddings are necessary. Do NOT re-propose dropping semantic retrieval for pure lexical — it's settled.

question: Does prepending model-generated per-chunk context improve recall@3, and can an on-device 1.5B generate it well enough?
lesson: Bounded run (25 contracts, 67 items, 2026-10-20): on-device Qwen2.5-1.5B-generated per-chunk context REDUCED recall@3 to 52.2% vs 62.7% standard baseline (-10.5 pts); static naive-prepend was flat (64.2%, CIs overlap). Harness validated (standard reproduces PoC-007 61.4%). Do NOT ship 1.5B-generated chunk context as a retrieval enhancement — it's a net regression at 6GB; the generic 'This chunk refers to...' preamble dilutes the embedding. CAVEAT: host-generator upper bound (H1) NOT run, so Anthropic's method-in-general is not disproven; n=67 wide CIs = suggestive not airtight. Full-corpus + host run deferred as optional. The hard-category bottleneck effort moved to PoC-014 (chunk boundaries) + PoC-015 (query formulation).

question: Is there a better semantic/BM25 weight than 0.7/0.3 for recall?
lesson: Swept semantic weight 0.1-0.9; recall rises monotonically to 58.1% at 0.9, +6.3 points over the 0.7 run, so ADOPTED a higher semantic weight. Caveats: the optimum sits at the edge of the tested range (retest >0.9 / pure-semantic before over-trusting 0.9); hard categories like Exclusivity (~11%) are weight-invariant, so weighting is not their bottleneck (chunking/question formulation is); and the 0.7 run here read 51.8% vs PoC-007's 61.4% baseline, so treat 013's absolute numbers as within-experiment. A plain 0.1-0.9 re-sweep is settled; extending the range or adaptive per-category weighting is still open.

question: Does clause/section-boundary chunking raise recall@3, especially on the weight-invariant hard categories?
lesson: Full corpus (1,325 items): clause chunking +2.5 overall (61.8->64.3, CIs OVERLAP, below +3 adopt bar). H2 REFUTED: hard categories barely moved (Non-Compete +4, Exclusivity +2 still 9%, Change-of-Control +0) -- the hard-category bottleneck is NOT chunk boundaries. H3 REFUTED: page already had 95.8% span-integrity (gold fits in one chunk), clause REDUCED it to 83.5%; the small gain is from more coherent retrieval units, not span containment. Clause gives a cheaper index (0.59x chunks) but not a recall win -> do not adopt. Combined with PoC-013 (scoring-invariant) and PoC-009 (depth-invariant), the remaining suspect for hard categories is the QUERY side (PoC-015) and cross-reference resolution (StrucChunk's untested half). Don't re-propose boundary-only chunking.

question: Do xref resolution and/or template question decomposition lift hard-category recall@3?
lesson: Full corpus (1,325 items). CROSS-REFERENCE RESOLUTION: reject -- appending referenced-clause text slightly HURT (-0.7 overall, -1.0 hard mean); dilutes the embedding like PoC-011 generated context. TEMPLATE QUESTION DECOMPOSITION (non-generative, 2-3 static sub-queries per hard category, union top-3): the signal -- overall +1.4, hard mean +6.0, and EXCLUSIVITY 7%->24% (+17), the FIRST mechanism across PoC 009/011/013/014 to move a hard category. Pre-registered +10 hard-mean bar not met (+6) so strictly inconclusive, but the per-category win is real and needs NO on-device generation (6GB-deployable). Combination xref+decomp showed no synergy (worse than decomp alone) -> drop. CONCLUSION: the hard-category bottleneck is a QUERY-FORMULATION problem (aligns with PoC-015), not chunking/scoring/depth. Follow-up: tune templates, extend categories, measure key-fact end-to-end. Don't re-propose cross-reference-append or boundary-only chunking for hard categories.

topic: query formulation (deterministic transforms) for hard/weak categories
question: Which deterministic query transform (gloss/keywords/decomposition) best lifts hard-category recall@3?
lesson: Arm A full corpus (1,325 items), chunks fixed=PoC014 page. KEYWORD EXPANSION (inject category's discriminative vocabulary) is the winner: +4.8 overall, +8.8 weak-cat mean, EXCLUSIVITY 7%->32% (beats decomposition's 7->24 and is cheaper, single query). Decomposition (PoC-016's mechanism) does NOT generalize (weak-mean +2.9, >=+10 on only 1/6 cats) -- the 016 win is really VOCABULARY INJECTION, which keywords do directly. Natural-language GLOSS HURTS (-2.0): fluency is not the lever, discriminative terms are. Liquidated Damages regressed under all transforms (raw already has right terms). CONCLUSION: hard-category bottleneck = query VOCABULARY MISMATCH; fix = inject category terms, not rephrase/generate/chunk. CAVEAT: recall@3 is a proxy -- Arm B (end-to-end key-fact, raw vs keywords on PoC 006 Qwen harness) NOT yet run; verdict holds H4 open. Also keywords boost BM25 arm too (part of gain may be lexical). Don't adopt into product retrieval until Arm B confirms conversion.
